bug_semantics: The advisory combines two x-proxy-path trust failures. In admin.ts, an attacker-controlled request header was inserted verbatim into served HTML, JavaScript, and CSS; because those header-dependent responses also lacked Vary and private/no-store cache controls, the reflection enabled direct or shared-cache-poisoning XSS on the admin origin. Separately, specialpages.ts passed a sanitizer that allowed leading slashes and then concatenated its result into a 302 Location. An x-proxy-path value of //evil.example therefore produced //evil.example/p/<encoded-pad>, which a browser follows as a protocol-relative cross-origin redirect.
flaw_origin: There are two independently introduced mechanisms. The admin reflection first appeared in human-authored commit 3e9c90e994d4af71ac8f49668f48caf61ef1b55d, not in the advisory's cited 63e9b2d4eb303cd341022591bdf9484584db36e3. The open-redirect mechanism first appeared when retained PR #7710 member f784c8c47c16e184b3ef3bdbf84485d4e5c42eb2 changed a safe relative redirect into an absolute redirect prefixed by sanitizeProxyPath(req), whose character filter preserved a leading //. That member was represented on the public branch by squash 451bd9c3ebb0dded99dd0ff21811ee00e0940c29. The selected introducer is the smallest BIC for the advisory's AI-authored open-redirect component; the separate older admin-XSS origin is retained for complete lifecycle attribution.

evidence: The assigned first-party GHSA-fjgc-3mj7-8rg8 / CVE-2026-55087 data identifies ep_etherpad-lite >=2.1.0 through 3.0.0 as affected, 3.1.0 as first patched, the admin body substitutions and legacy-timeslider redirect as the two sinks, and PR #7784 as the fixing PR.

git log -L and -S history reported by both blind audits identifies 3e9c90e994d4af71ac8f49668f48caf61ef1b55d as the first admin.ts raw-header substitutions, absent from its parent e6e1af58104b16a41fb500899e9a0bb50a7d1b85. The adjudication re-check `git show --format=%H%n%P%n%s --name-status 63e9b2d4eb303cd341022591bdf9484584db36e3` shows that advisory-cited commit touched APIHandler.ts, Settings.ts, tsort.js, and pnpm-lock.yaml, not admin.ts, so it is rejected as this sink's BIC.

`git diff c5a54cfd7b528186aca33aea971b7099ca468790 f784c8c47c16e184b3ef3bdbf84485d4e5c42eb2 -- src/node/hooks/express/specialpages.ts` shows the sole causal change: the parent used only `../${encodeURIComponent(req.params.pad)}`, while the child reads sanitizeProxyPath(req) and emits `${proxyPath}/p/${encodeURIComponent(req.params.pad)}`. `git show --format= --name-status` shows that BIC modifies only specialpages.ts. The direct parent therefore lacks the header-controlled Location sink.

`git diff --exit-code f784c8c47c16e184b3ef3bdbf84485d4e5c42eb2 451bd9c3ebb0dded99dd0ff21811ee00e0940c29 -- src/node/hooks/express/specialpages.ts` is empty, proving the retained member's file state is the one represented by the squash. `git tag --contains 451bd9c3ebb0dded99dd0ff21811ee00e0940c29` starts at 3.0.0/v3.0.0. The squash aggregate is used only for public shipment, not substituted for the smaller BIC.

`git cat-file -p f784c8c47c16e184b3ef3bdbf84485d4e5c42eb2` records sole parent c5a54cfd7b528186aca33aea971b7099ca468790, human author/committer John McLear, and the exact Claude Opus 4.7 Co-Authored-By trailer. This BIC commit object is the only AI-attribution source.

The assigned fix_sha disagreement is narrower than its label: both blind reports chose public squash fix 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996, but the primary chose direct member a6de73c8f90a75289de35f7585165a361ba54f28 while the reviewer chose 714f66caa139849660fac3aa826b4dff2468e65e. `git cat-file -p` shows 714f66caa139849660fac3aa826b4dff2468e65e and a6de73c8f90a75289de35f7585165a361ba54f28 have the same parent b96e262782e1ed72999c42cb47fb9140e58fe544, subject, and author timestamp but different trees and a later committer timestamp for a6de73c8f90a75289de35f7585165a361ba54f28, making them rewritten alternatives rather than sequential fixes.

`git diff 714f66caa139849660fac3aa826b4dff2468e65e a6de73c8f90a75289de35f7585165a361ba54f28` shows that the later replacement adds the sanitizer's absolute-prefix guarantee and related tests, among other amendments. Contrary to the review claim, 714f66caa139849660fac3aa826b4dff2468e65e does not contain the `if (cleaned[0] !== '/') cleaned = '/' + cleaned` behavior that the reviewer attributed to it.

`git cat-file -p 29fd3b3638f60342da34bcf4a3bd2c8c269e7e1` records a6de73c8f90a75289de35f7585165a361ba54f28 as the PR head's direct parent. `git diff --exit-code a6de73c8f90a75289de35f7585165a361ba54f28 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996 -- src/node/hooks/express/admin.ts src/node/hooks/express/specialpages.ts src/node/utils/sanitizeProxyPath.ts src/tests/backend/specs/proxyPathRedirect.ts src/tests/backend-new/specs/sanitizeProxyPath.test.ts` is empty, while the equivalent 714f66caa139849660fac3aa826b4dff2468e65e-to-squash comparison differs in sanitizeProxyPath.ts and its tests. This resolves direct_fix_sha for the primary and rejects the reviewer's superseded object.

`git diff b96e262782e1ed72999c42cb47fb9140e58fe544 a6de73c8f90a75289de35f7585165a361ba54f28` over the three production paths shows the direct fix replacing raw admin substitutions with the shared sanitizer, adding Vary: x-proxy-path and Cache-Control: private, no-store, collapsing multiple leading slashes, forcing one leading slash, rejecting traversal, and changing specialpages.ts to import the shared helper. The same path diff against public squash 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996 is identical. The squash is therefore the public fix_sha, while a6de73c8f90a75289de35f7585165a361ba54f28 is the final direct fixing member.

`git tag --contains 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996` starts at 3.1.0/v3.1.0 and excludes 3.0.0. `git rev-parse` resolves 3.0.0/v3.0.0 to 149c6a24e73761fc06bc9e61b93bc04be6bc044e and 3.1.0/v3.1.0 to fa1c6b2e43d0510c851643cb7ba67cf042331a37. The 3.0.0 specialpages.ts tree retains the vulnerable header-prefixed redirect; the 3.1.0 tree imports the shared sanitizer, whose tree collapses leading /{2,} and forces a single leading slash, and admin.ts has the sanitizer plus cache headers. This independently matches the advisory's <=3.0.0/3.1.0 boundary.
reasoning: Vulnerability-first tracing separates the GHSA's two causal paths. The admin XSS/cache-poisoning sink is human-authored and begins before v2.1.0. For the open redirect, public commit 451bd9c3ebb0dded99dd0ff21811ee00e0940c29 is a squash aggregate, so it is rejected as the BIC; retained one-file member f784c8c47c16e184b3ef3bdbf84485d4e5c42eb2 is the smallest change that first feeds the slash-preserving sanitizer into Location, and its immediate parent retains the safe relative form. Its own commit object, not any later object, explicitly co-attributes Claude, so the open-redirect component meets AI_ROOT_CAUSE without misattributing the independently human-origin admin component. On the assigned fix_sha topic, both prior reports were right that 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996 is the public squash fix. The actual disagreement was direct_fix_sha. The primary wins: a6de73c8f90a75289de35f7585165a361ba54f28 is the amended PR member directly parented by the retained PR head and its relevant trees exactly match the landed squash. The reviewer's 714f66caa139849660fac3aa826b4dff2468e65e is a superseded rewrite sibling, not the retained direct member, and its sanitizer lacks behavior the review claimed it contained. Public squash 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996 first appears in 3.1.0, closing both advisory mechanisms after the vulnerable 3.0.0 state.
